# Foundation cracks and basement moisture

A homeowner's guide to what the basement walls are telling you.

## Hairline cracks

A thin vertical crack, narrower than 1/8 inch, in a poured concrete wall is usually shrinkage from curing and is cosmetic. Seal it with an epoxy or polyurethane injection kit, and mark the ends with a pencil to see if it grows.

## Cracks that signal structural movement

Be worried about horizontal cracks, stair-step cracks along the mortar of a block wall, cracks wider than 1/4 inch, a wall that bows inward, or doors and windows that suddenly stick. These point to soil pressure or settlement. Call a structural engineer before a contractor, because the fix depends on the cause.

## Moisture and white powder

A white chalky powder on the wall is efflorescence, mineral salts left behind as water passes through. It means moisture, not a structural failure. Fix the water first, then clean the wall with a stiff brush and vinegar solution.

## Drainage and gutters

Most wet basements are a drainage problem. Keep the gutters clear, send downspouts at least 6 feet from the house, and slope the soil away from the foundation.

## Sump pumps

A sump pump moves water out of the pit before it rises. Test it each spring by pouring in a bucket of water, and consider a battery backup for storms.
